question: Why did it fall so much along the way?
answer:
The fall was probably a combination of a broad risk-off market move and DOCN-specific concerns about how quickly its growth could continue, rather than one single event.

In this run, the worst drawdown began on February 18, 2025, when the portfolio value was $1,747, and ended on August 1, 2025, at $963. That was a 44.9% decline, or $784. The timing overlaps a broader February market selloff tied to disappointing U.S. economic data, as reported in this contemporaneous market recap: [February market selloff and DOCN volatility](https://markets.financialcontent.com/pennwell.bioopticsworld/article/stockstory-2025-2-24-why-digitalocean-docn-stock-is-falling-today).

DOCN’s own results were not uniformly bad. Its February 25 report for the prior quarter was described as strong, with positive full-year guidance, so it does not explain the initial February 18 start. However, the stock still had a high-growth valuation and was volatile, making it vulnerable when investors questioned future growth or reduced exposure to riskier technology stocks.

The May earnings reaction is a clearer DOCN-specific example. DigitalOcean reported a quarterly revenue and earnings beat, but the shares still fell in premarket trading. The market appeared more focused on forward growth expectations and positioning than on the backward-looking results, as described in this [Q1 2025 earnings reaction](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-digitalocean-q1-2025-earnings-beat-forecasts-stock-dips-93CH-4025019).

The later recovery also matters. The portfolio eventually reached its highest value of $6,784 on June 15, 2026, and ended the tested period at $4,899. So the drawdown was severe along the way, but it did not prevent the buy-and-hold position from recovering and finishing strongly. The run does not provide a daily breakdown that can assign a precise portion of the $784 decline to each news event.
